description: This module creates, modifies, and deletes VPN connections.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: connection_type
parameters.description: The type of VPN connection. At this time only ipsec.1 is supported. Default: "ipsec.1"

parameters.name: customer_gateway_id
parameters.description: The ID of the customer gateway.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: The time, in seconds, to wait before checking operation again. Default: 15

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: An alternative to using vpn_connection_id. If multiple matches are found, vpn_connection_id is required. If one of the following suboptions is a list of items to filter by, only one item needs to match to find the VPN that correlates. e.g. if the filter filters.cidr is ["194.168.2.0/24", "192.168.2.0/24"] and the VPN route only has the destination cidr block of 192.168.2.0/24 it will be found with this filter (assuming there are not multiple VPNs that are matched). Another example, if the filter filters.vpn is equal to ["vpn-ccf7e7ad", "vpn-cb0ae2a2"] and one of of the VPNs has the state deleted (exists but is unmodifiable) and the other exists and is not deleted, it will be found via this filter. Default: {}

parameters.name: bgp
parameters.description: The BGP ASN number associated with a BGP device. Only works if the connection is attached. This filtering option is currently not working.

parameters.name: cgw
parameters.description: The customer gateway id as a string or a list of those strings.

parameters.name: cgw-config
parameters.description: The customer gateway configuration of the VPN as a string (in the format of the return value) or a list of those strings.

parameters.name: cidr
parameters.description: The destination cidr of the VPN’s route as a string or a list of those strings.

parameters.name: static-routes-only
parameters.description: The type of routing; true or false. Choices: false true

parameters.name: tag-keys
parameters.description: The key of a tag as a string or a list of those strings.

parameters.name: tag-values
parameters.description: The value of a tag as a string or a list of those strings.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: A dict of key value pairs.

parameters.name: vgw
parameters.description: The virtual private gateway as a string or a list of those strings.

parameters.name: vpn
parameters.description: The VPN connection id as a string or a list of those strings.

parameters.name: local_ipv4_network_cidr
parameters.description: The IPv4 CIDR on the customer gateway (on-premises) side of the VPN connection. Default: "0.0.0.0/0"

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: purge_routes
parameters.description: Whether or not to delete VPN connections routes that are not specified in the task. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: purge_tags
parameters.description: If purge_tags=true and tags is set, existing tags will be purged from the resource to match exactly what is defined by tags parameter. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified, even if purge_tags=True. Tag keys beginning with aws: are reserved by Amazon and can not be modified. As such they will be ignored for the purposes of the purge_tags parameter. See the Amazon documentation for more information https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_tagging.html#tag-conventions. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: routes
parameters.description: Routes to add to the connection. Default: []

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The desired state of the VPN connection. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: static_only
parameters.description: Indicates whether the VPN connection uses static routes only. Static routes must be used for devices that don’t support BGP. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: transit_gateway_id
parameters.description: The ID of the transit gateway. Mutually exclusive with vpn_gateway_id.

parameters.name: tunnel_options
parameters.description: An optional list object containing no more than two dict members, each of which may contain tunnel_options.TunnelInsideCidr and/or tunnel_options.PreSharedKey keys with appropriate string values. AWS defaults will apply in absence of either of the aforementioned keys. Default: []

parameters.name: PreSharedKey
parameters.description: The pre-shared key (PSK) to establish initial authentication between the virtual private gateway and customer gateway.

parameters.name: TunnelInsideCidr
parameters.description: The range of inside IPv4 addresses for the tunnel.

parameters.name: TunnelInsideIpv6Cidr
parameters.description: The range of inside IPv6 addresses for the tunnel.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: vpn_connection_id
parameters.description: The ID of the VPN connection. Required to modify or delete a connection if the filters option does not provide a unique match.

parameters.name: vpn_gateway_id
parameters.description: The ID of the virtual private gateway. Mutually exclusive with transit_gateway_id.

parameters.name: wait_timeout
parameters.description: How long, in seconds, before wait gives up. Default: 600

examples:
# Note: These examples do not set authentication details, see the AWS Guide for details.

- name: Create a VPN connection with vpn_gateway_id
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "present"
    vpn_gateway_id: "vgw-XXXXXXXX"
    customer_gateway_id: "cgw-XXXXXXXX"

- name: Attach a vpn connection to transit gateway
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "present"
    transit_gateway_id: "tgw-XXXXXXXX"
    customer_gateway_id: "cgw-XXXXXXXX"

- name: Modify VPN connection tags
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "present"
    vpn_connection_id: "vpn-XXXXXXXX"
    tags:
      Name: "ansible-tag-1"
      Other: "ansible-tag-2"

- name: Delete a connection
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    vpn_connection_id: "vpn-XXXXXXXX"
    state: "absent"

- name: Modify VPN tags (identifying VPN by filters)
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "present"
    filters:
      cidr: "194.168.1.0/24"
      tag-keys:
        - "Ansible"
        - "Other"
    tags:
      New: "Tag"
    purge_tags: true
    static_only: true

- name: Set up VPN with tunnel options utilizing 'TunnelInsideCidr' only
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "present"
    filters:
      vpn: "vpn-XXXXXXXX"
    static_only: true
    tunnel_options:
      - TunnelInsideCidr: "169.254.100.1/30"
      - TunnelInsideCidr: "169.254.100.5/30"

- name: Add routes and remove any preexisting ones
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "present"
    filters:
      vpn: "vpn-XXXXXXXX"
    routes:
      - "195.168.2.0/24"
      - "196.168.2.0/24"
    purge_routes: true

- name: Remove all routes
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "present"
    vpn_connection_id: "vpn-XXXXXXXX"
    routes: []
    purge_routes: true

- name: Delete a VPN identified by filters
  amazon.aws.ec2_vpc_vpn:
    state: "absent"
    filters:
      tags:
        Ansible: "Tag"

return_values.name: changed
return_values.description: If the VPN connection has changed. Returned: always Sample: true

return_values.name: customer_gateway_configuration
return_values.description: The configuration of the VPN connection. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: customer_gateway_id
return_values.description: The customer gateway connected via the connection. Returned: state=present Sample: "cgw-1220c87b"

return_values.name: gateway_association_state
return_values.description: The current state of the gateway association. Returned: state=present Sample: "associated"

return_values.name: options
return_values.description: The VPN connection options. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: enable_acceleration
return_values.description: Indicates whether acceleration is enabled for the VPN connection. Returned: state=present Sample: false

return_values.name: local_ipv4_network_cidr
return_values.description: The IPv4 CIDR on the customer gateway (on-premises) side of the VPN connection. Returned: state=present Sample: "0.0.0.0/0"

return_values.name: outside_ip_address_type
return_values.description: The external IP address of the VPN tunnel. Returned: state=present Sample: "PublicIpv4"

return_values.name: remote_ipv4_network_cidr
return_values.description: The IPv4 CIDR on the Amazon Web Services side of the VPN connection. Returned: state=present Sample: "0.0.0.0/0"

return_values.name: static_routes_only
return_values.description: If the VPN connection only allows static routes. Returned: state=present Sample: true

return_values.name: tunnel_inside_ip_version
return_values.description: Indicates whether the VPN tunnels process IPv4 or IPv6 traffic. Returned: state=present Sample: "ipv4"

return_values.name: tunnel_options
return_values.description: Indicates the VPN tunnel options. Returned: state=present Sample: [{"log_options": {"cloud_watch_log_options": {"log_enabled": false}}, "outside_ip_address": "34.225.101.10", "pre_shared_key": "8n7hnjNE8zhIt4VpMOIfcrw6XnUTHLW9", "tunnel_inside_cidr": "169.254.31.8/30"}]

return_values.name: log_options
return_values.description: Options for logging VPN tunnel activity. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: cloud_watch_log_options
return_values.description: Options for sending VPN tunnel logs to CloudWatch. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: outside_ip_address
return_values.description: The external IP address of the VPN tunnel. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: pre_shared_key
return_values.description: The pre-shared key (PSK) to establish initial authentication between the virtual private gateway and the customer gateway. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: tunnel_inside_cidr
return_values.description: The range of inside IPv4 addresses for the tunnel. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: routes
return_values.description: The routes of the VPN connection. Returned: state=present Sample: [{"destination_cidr_block": "192.168.1.0/24", "state": "available"}]

return_values.name: destination_cidr_block
return_values.description: The CIDR block associated with the local subnet of the customer data center. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: source
return_values.description: Indicates how the routes were provided. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: state
return_values.description: The current state of the static route. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: The tags associated with the connection. Returned: state=present Sample: {"name": "ansible-test", "other": "tag"}

return_values.name: transit_gateway_id
return_values.description: The transit gateway id to which the vpn connection can be attached. Returned: state=present Sample: "tgw-cb0ae2a2"

return_values.name: type
return_values.description: The type of VPN connection (currently only ipsec.1 is available). Returned: state=present Sample: "ipsec.1"

return_values.name: vgw_telemetry
return_values.description: The telemetry for the VPN tunnel. Returned: state=present Sample: [{"accepted_route_count": 0, "last_status_change": "2024-09-30T13:12:33+00:00", "outside_ip_address": "34.225.101.10", "status": "DOWN", "status_message": "IPSEC IS DOWN"}]

return_values.name: accepted_route_count
return_values.description: The number of accepted routes. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: certificate_arn
return_values.description: The Amazon Resource Name of the virtual private gateway tunnel endpoint certificate. Returned: when a private certificate is used for authentication Sample: "arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate/c544d8ce-20b8-4fff-98b0-example"

return_values.name: last_status_change
return_values.description: The date and time of the last change in status. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: status
return_values.description: The status of the VPN tunnel. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: status_message
return_values.description: If an error occurs, a description of the error. Returned: state=present

return_values.name: vpn_connection_id
return_values.description: The identifier for the VPN connection. Returned: state=present Sample: "vpn-781e0e19"

return_values.name: vpn_gateway_id
return_values.description: The virtual private gateway connected via the connection. Returned: state=present Sample: "vgw-cb0ae2a2"
